description.text: CACI International Inc (CACI), a Delaware corporation, is a holding company whose operations are conducted through subsidiaries primarily located in the U.S. and Europe. CACI was founded in 1962 as a simulation technology company and has grown into a leading provider of differentiated Technology and distinctive Expertise to customers in support of national security in the intelligence, defense, and federal civilian sectors, both domestically and internationally. Unless the context indicates otherwise, the terms “CACI,” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our,” refer to CACI International Inc and its subsidiaries and joint ventures that are majority-owned or otherwise controlled by it. The term “the Registrant” refers to CACI International Inc only. •Technology – CACI provides technology that addresses our customers’ most challenging needs. This includes agile software development using open modern architectures and DevSecOps; advanced data platforms, applications, and analytics augmented by Artificial Intelligence (AI), Enterprise Resource Planning systems, electromagnetic spectrum capabilities, space-based sensors and ground site processors, photonics, and network modernization. CACI invests ahead of customer need with research and development (R&D) to create unique and differentiated technology addressing critical national security needs. •Expertise – CACI delivers talent with the specific technical and functional knowledge to support agency operations.

about.description_short: CACI International Inc (NYSE: CACI) is a technology-first national security company that expands the limits of national security through innovation, discipline, and operational excellence. We deliver advanced technologies that help our customers move faster, operate more efficiently, and anticipate and defeat evolving threats. Our 27,000 talented employees and strong culture drive our success and have earned CACI recognition as a Fortune World's Most Admired Company. CACI is a member of the Fortune 500, the Russell 1000 Index, and the S&P MidCap 400 Index. For more information, visit caci.com.

analysis_md:
# CACI — CACI International Inc
Pass-1 v5 run, 2026-10-17 (engine release 5.4.0). Fiscal year ends June 30; latest FY is FY2026 ended 2026-06-30 (3.6 months ago — not stale; ttm.py confirms no 10-Q has been filed since the FY end, so FY2026 is the TTM period).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json or the cited FY2026 earnings release — none are recomputed.

## What it is
US national-security technology and services contractor (Reston, VA): mission IT, DevSecOps, SIGINT, electronic warfare and space-based sensing for the Department of Defense and the intelligence community, ~90% national-security work with federal civilian exposure largely exited. FY2026 revenue $9,567,779,000 (+10.89% YoY, of which 7.2% organic per the earnings release), operating margin 9.6%, EBITDA margin 12.3%. Total backlog $32.0B with funded backlog up 29% YoY and FY2026 contract awards of $10.2B (book-to-bill 1.1x) per the earnings release. On 2026-03-09 CACI closed the all-cash $2.6B acquisition of ARKA Group (space-based EO/IR sensors, hyperspectral imaging, agentic-AI geospatial software; ~1,100 employees), debt-funded — the defining event of the fiscal year.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2026 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $886,710,000; capex $106,653,000; SBC $79,514,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2026: $700,543,000 = $31.59/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $31.59, latest FY OE total $700.5M)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $455,809,000 — materially below the conservative figure, and here the maintenance version is the distorted one: the engine's D&A tag captures $77,600,000 of depreciation while the FY2026 cash-flow statement's depreciation-and-amortization line is $245,899,000 (earnings release), so the maintenance add-back is understated. The conservative OCF-based figure is the series used throughout.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but volatile per share: FY2022 $27.00, FY2023 $12.16, FY2024 $16.82, FY2025 $18.81, FY2026 $31.59 (financials_history.csv). OCF margin has swung between roughly 6% and 12% of revenue across the decade on working-capital timing (receivables build in high-growth years, MARPA receivables-facility timing, tax timing).
- Net debt $4.710B (key_numbers.md) — see HIGH_NET_DEBT below. Share count is shrinking: diluted shares 22,176,000, share count CAGR −1.79%/yr (already credited in the growth blend).

**Base used = $22.4079/share via base_override — the simple mean of the last three filed FY OE/share prints.** See OVERRIDE.

## OVERRIDE — base (bounded authority (c))
- **The problem (BASE_DIVERGENCE):** latest FY OE/share $31.59 vs the engine's normalized 3-yr median $18.81 — both are distorted, in opposite directions.
  - The **latest FY is flattered**: deferred income taxes added $145,387,000 to FY2026 OCF (vs −$27,060,000 in FY2025, FY2026 earnings-release cash-flow statement) as the ARKA purchase-accounting deferred tax liability built (deferred income taxes on the balance sheet rose from $142,636,000 to $376,580,000); working-capital drag eased (receivables build of $198,983,000 vs $269,215,000 in FY2025) on what the release calls efficient working capital management; and ARKA contributed only a ~4-month stub of earnings against the enlarged capital base.
  - The **median is depressed**: it is the FY2025 print, from the low-OCF-margin years (FY2024–25 OCF ran ~6.5% / ~6.3% of revenue, the low end of the decade range, while receivables built through 14–15% revenue-growth years), and it assigns zero weight to the ARKA step-up — which FY2027 guidance corroborates (free cash flow of at least $900M guided for FY2027, per the earnings release, vs the $735M the company reported for FY2026).
- **The decision:** judgment.json carries `base_override = {value: 22.4079, source: "This run's financials_history.csv / dcf_numbers.json OE-per-share prints: FY2024 $16.8228, FY2025 $18.8107, FY2026 $31.5901; mean of the three", reason: (full text in judgment.json)}` — built exclusively from figures this run's engine outputs printed, under bounded authority (c). The mean splits the two distortions instead of picking either extreme.
- **Measured impact (engine `--measure` runs, all other inputs at default):** median base → weighted IRR 8.22%, IV@15% $259.93, Tier D; mean base → 9.23%, $309.64, Tier D; latest-FY base → 11.71%, $436.52, Tier C. **No defensible base clears 15%** — the verdict does not rest on the override. The final run (below) pairs the mean base with guidance-calibrated growth and prints 8.16% / $262.33.
- The override is recorded in score.json and in the central registry (_system/overrides_registry.json).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: classified incumbency, a cleared workforce and differentiated owned technology are real advantages, but through-cycle returns on capital are unremarkable and every contract is eventually recomped.
- **ROIC evidence (fundamentals.json `roic_proxy` series):** FY2017 6.6%, FY2018 8.7%, FY2019 7.7%, FY2020 9.3%, FY2021 11.5%, FY2022 8.6%, FY2023 9.4%, FY2024 10.2%, FY2025 9.4%, FY2026 7.6% — a decade spent barely above the cost of capital, with FY2026 diluted by the ARKA capital base. That record does not support a moat above 5. CACI does not file a usable gross-margin line in recent years (fundamentals.json gross margin is null from FY2020 on; cost of revenue absorbs direct labor), so the margin evidence is the operating margin trend: 8.0% (FY2022) → 8.5% → 8.5% → 8.9% → 9.6% (FY2026) — real mix improvement, from a low base.
- FOR: classified incumbency and cleared workforce — high barriers to entry on intelligence / DoD mission programs; differentiated owned technology (SIGINT, electronic warfare, space-based sensors via ARKA) vs pure labor-hour services; $32.0B total backlog (~3.3x FY2026 revenue), funded backlog +29% YoY, FY2026 book-to-bill 1.1x; mix shift to technology lifting operating margin 8.0% → 9.6% and EBITDA margin to 12.3%; ~90% national-security concentration in enduring, well-funded budget priorities.
- AGAINST: ROIC proxy only 7.6–11.5% over the last decade — no wide-moat economics; contracts recompete — incumbency is rented, not owned, and Leidos, Booz Allen, GDIT, SAIC and Peraton bid the same task orders; single-customer complex — US federal budgets, procurement delays, shutdowns and administration priorities set demand; people-based delivery limits pricing power; growth partly acquired, not organic (ARKA $2.6B cash; FY2026 revenue +10.9% total vs +7.2% organic).
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-17)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended growth is 13.54%, but one blend component is an artifact — OE/share CAGR 2y of 37.06% measures the depressed FY2024 base to the flattered FY2026 print, straddling both distortions and the ARKA close. The revenue components (5y CAGR 9.62%, 3y CAGR 12.59%, latest YoY 10.89%) and FY2027 guidance (revenue $10.65–10.85B, +11.3–13.4% total but only +6.1–8.2% organic; adjusted EPS guided $32.96–33.86 vs $29.83 in FY2026; FCF at least $900M — earnings release) center OE/share growth nearer 10%. Scenario starts were therefore set via offsets (−0.1204 / −0.0704 / −0.0304 / +0.0146 / +0.0596 vs the blend) to 1.5 / 6.5 / **10.5** / 15.0 / 19.5%. The bull start (15.0%) sits *below* the latest total revenue print (Q4 FY2026 revenue +17.6% YoY) with a written reason: that print is flattered by the ARKA stub step-up, FY2027 total revenue guidance caps at +13.4%, and bull-case OE/share growth above the revenue guide must come from buybacks, margin and deleveraging rather than revenue. Probabilities were skewed one notch bearish (10/30/30/20/10 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) for the leverage below; OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $614.31.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | 1.5% | 0.75 | Recompete losses + budget freeze; levered OE compresses on $4.9B debt | $132.16 | 5.16% |
| Bear | 30% | 6.5% | 0.90 | Organic-guide growth only; ARKA integration drags; WC tailwind reverses | $195.22 | 6.61% |
| Base | 30% | 10.5% | 1.00 | FY2027 guidance trajectory decays normally over the CAP | $255.83 | 7.98% |
| Bull | 20% | 15.0% | 1.10 | ARKA full-year + EW/space award momentum; margin keeps climbing | $338.31 | 9.78% |
| Super bull | 10% | 19.5% | 1.25 | Sustained double-digit growth + rapid deleveraging | $461.32 | 12.24% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $262.33 (−57.3% vs price), IV@12% $353.30, IV@10% $455.31, weighted IRR 8.16%, base-case IRR 7.98%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Bear tier D, bull tier D — even the super-bull scenario (12.24%) does not clear 15% at this price. Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 3.65%, terminal value 20.1% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.49x, net debt 9.48x normalized OE, 3.6 months since FY end.
- **Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $262.33 · 20% at $181.29 · 25% at $137.23.**

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $31.59 vs 3-yr median $18.81): resolved in OVERRIDE — both are distorted (latest flattered by ARKA-year deferred taxes of $145,387,000 in OCF, eased working-capital drag and a stub contribution; median depressed by the low-OCF-margin FY2024–25 years and blind to ARKA). Mean base used; measured impact shows the tier is D on the median and the mean, C only on the flattered latest FY.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 9.48x normalized OE on the final base; preliminary run: 11.3x on the median base): balance sheet from the filing (financials_history.csv FY2026): total debt $4,901,509,000 (long-term $4,854,759,000), cash $191,756,000, net debt $4,709,753,000, plus lease liabilities $483,024,000. The debt is the ARKA deal: $2.6B all-cash, closed 2026-03-09, funded with borrowings (long-term debt was $2,849,190,000 at FY2025). Management reported pro forma leverage of 3.7x EBITDA at Q4 and guided to the low-3s by June 2027 (earnings call, via search results) — a credible deleveraging path given guided FCF of at least $900M, but at 9.48x normalized OE the equity is a levered stub: stressed in the scenarios via the 0.75/0.90 bear-side OE multipliers and a 40% combined bear-or-worse probability weight.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (preliminary run: super-bull IV 4.4x super-bear IV): real in the preliminary run because it paired the depressed median base with the artifact-inflated 13.54% blend. Recalibrating the base and growth narrowed the final spread to 3.49x (key_numbers.md), which is still wide — confidence is capped at medium, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the *range*: Tier D on the median and normalized-mean bases, Tier C on the flattered latest-FY base. No method clears the 15% hurdle at $614.31 — the market is pricing CACI as if FY2026's cash conversion and double-digit growth are the permanent run-rate, and paying for the ARKA step-up in full, in advance.
- Quality is not the debate: OE-positive 5/5 years, backlog ~3.3x revenue, funded backlog +29%, margins expanding, buybacks shrinking the count. The debate is price and leverage: an OE yield of 3.65% on the normalized base, with net debt at 9.48x that base, leaves no margin of safety — the bear IV@15% ($195.22) sits at roughly a third of the price.
- Watch items for pass 2: whether FY2027 OCF confirms the ≥$900M FCF guide without another deferred-tax tailwind; ARKA revenue/ROIC as a full year consolidates (FY2026 ROIC proxy fell to 7.6% on the enlarged capital base); pace of deleveraging vs the low-3s-by-June-2027 guide; funded-backlog conversion.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.16% on the final inputs; method range D to C across defensible bases)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filing data and on the conclusion — no base clears 15% — medium-low on any single IV point estimate given the 3.49x scenario spread and the leverage)
- One-liner: Solid defense-tech compounder, moat 5/10 — but at $614.31 it does not clear 15% on any defensible base (weighted IRR 8.2%, IV@15% $262.33 on the normalized base; even the flattered latest-FY base prints only Tier C); it would need to fall to ~$262 to clear the 15% hurdle.
